newsitem.title: USA: Collins & Aikman buys some Perstorp opers.
newsitem.headline: Collins & Aikman buys some Perstorp opers.

text.p: Collins & Aikman Corp said on Wednesday it had acquired Perstorp AB's automotive supply and related operations in North America, the United Kingdom and Spain for $108 million, subject to post-closing adjustment.
The company said it acquired three Perstorp Components facilities in the United States, two in Canada, one in Mexico, three in the U.K. and one in Spain.
Funds for the acquisition came from its existing revolving credit facility, the company said.
In addition, the two companies entered into a joint venture agreement relating to Perstorp's automotive components supply facilities in Sweden, Belgium and France.
Each company will invest $7.5 million in cash and have a 49.9 percent interest in the joint venture, which will be managed by Collins & Aikman, it said.

The joint venture will purchase the Perstorp components business in Sweden, Belgium and France for $67 million, of which $15 million will be the equity investment and about $52 million of will be debt, the company said. The indebtedness will initially be held by Perstorp but is expected to be refinanced with new bank debt, which Perstorp is arranging. Collins & Aikman said it will not have any liability for the new bank financing.

The joint venture agreement includes an option for Collins & Aikman to purchase Perstorp's equity interest in the joint venture at a predetermined multiple of future cash flow for a period of three years.
After this, Perstorp would have a two-year purchase right if Collins & Aikman had not exercised its purchase right.
